title: Bombing cities
hook: Selected attacks brought destruction to urban populations.
notes: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed. Sources by scene: 1. London: the sustained Blitz begins: https://historicengland.org.uk/whats-new/features/blitz-stories/england-under-attack/; 2. Coventry: destruction and a surviving ruin: https://www.coventrycathedral.org.uk/locations/the-ruins; 3. Dresden: an Allied attack: https://www.dhm.de/lemo/kapitel/zweiter-weltkrieg/kriegsverlauf/dresden; 4. Hiroshima: an atomic bombing: https://www.archives.gov/news/topics/hiroshima-nagasaki-75; 5. Nagasaki: a second atomic bombing: https://www.archives.gov/news/topics/hiroshima-nagasaki-75 Nagasaki terrain and damage context: Manhattan Engineer District, The Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1946), chapter 9, https://www.atomicarchive.com/resources/documents/med/med_chp9.html (primary report transcription; no numerical damage claims imported).

scenes.title: London: the sustained Blitz begins
scenes.text: The sustained Blitz on London began on 7 September 1940. Bombing damaged homes and infrastructure and killed civilians. The point locates London, without implying that all attacks struck one site or covered the entire city uniformly.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1938 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: Coventry: destruction and a surviving ruin
scenes.text: The Luftwaffe attacked Coventry on the night of 14 November 1940. The cathedral was destroyed; its ruins remain a witness to the raid. This point locates the city rather than an invented bomb-impact grid.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1938 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: Dresden: an Allied attack
scenes.text: British bombing on the night of 13–14 February 1945 devastated Dresden, followed by US attacks. Naming the attackers matters when mapping civilian destruction. This city point does not estimate a firestorm perimeter or select among disputed casualty totals.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1945 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: Hiroshima: an atomic bombing
scenes.text: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. The National Archives documents destruction and large-scale loss of life. This point locates the city; it does not model a blast-radius circle or assign a precise death total.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1945 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: Nagasaki: a second atomic bombing
scenes.text: The United States bombed Nagasaki on 9 August 1945. The two cities experienced different terrain and attack conditions. This chapter identifies the dates and cities without treating them as interchangeable casualty measurements.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1945 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)
